note: Prompts for a card in a position, keyed by the position's key and the card's number. A card with no prompt falls back to its gloss, so this fills in at whatever pace the writing goes. Relations are sentence templates with an {other} slot; shadow has self and other variants because direction matters.

serves.11: Serves the Judge the way a good soldier serves an order: without needing the reason, and willing to say it out loud in company.
serves.15: Serves the Dancer in company, and knows what every room in the port is buying. Whatever they are for, they are charming about it.
serves.33: Acts for the Deckhand the way rock acts on the crews who work it: patiently, and without negotiating. They keep the people everyone else wrote off.

surface.24: The port knows them as the one with money, which brings work and no friends. Nobody has asked how the ledger got that way.
surface.65: The port blames them for a run of bad luck, and they have stopped correcting anyone. The rumour arrives before they do.

want.43: Wants something that is not theirs, and has already worked out how to take it. The only question left is whether the crew is in the way.
want.54: Wants a thing they heard once, in a place they cannot describe, and wants the crew to come and hear it too.

secret.11: Hides that the orders came from somewhere they will not name. The discipline is real. So is the thing they were told not to say.
secret.36: Keeps a tune the whole port sings. What they hide is that the song is a message, and they are the only one who does not know who it is for.

owed.45: They are owed by chance itself, and will tell you so at the table. Whoever they talk into the bet ends up owing something too.
owed.63: Someone with weight owes them, and would rather settle in coin than in kind. Coin can be refused, which is why they ask for it.

shadow.self: Shadow of the {other}: the same Icon, once where it can be seen and once where it cannot. What you answered there is also true here.
shadow.other: Casts a shadow on the {other}: the same Icon, said again where it cannot be seen.

relations.echo: Echoes the {other}: the Icon comes back unhidden, so the crew will recognise it before the character admits it.
relations.pair: Pairs with the {other}: two cards of the same Icon, read as one answer.
